findings: § 2 Prop. 2's finding (DEC-122) CARRIED OVER to the Énoncé (DEC-127), not a failure of F: the printed Énoncé (l.554–558, p. 241), read over all Hausdorff connected affine conical manifolds with « variétés » (Hausdorff, plan F6) on the projective side, is false in every Benzécri dimension n ≥ 3 whatever the reading of « isomorphisme », because among those cones the essential image of F on Hausdorff bases is exactly the cones with a proper ℝ₊*-action (Benzecri.exists_iso_coneObj_iff): Cone/Counterexample's ConeCex.VDim m (Hausdorff, second countable, connected) is isomorphic to no F(B) with B Hausdorff (Benzecri.not_essSurjAsPrinted_dim, against the Prop Benzecri.EssSurjAsPrintedDim). It IS F of its own base (Benzecri.ConeCex.isoFConeBase: V ≅ F(V/ℝ₊*) holds for every Hausdorff cone, no Hausdorff base needed), and that base is not Hausdorff (Benzecri.ConeCex.not_t2Space_coneBase_dim); both at once: Benzecri.ConeCex.iso_FCone_coneBase_and_not_t2Space. In dimension n ≤ 2 the printed form holds (Benzecri.essSurjAsPrinted_of_le_one).

F(B) always has a proper ℝ₊*-action and a Hausdorff base (FCone.properSMul, FCone.t2Space_coneBase): the construction of the proof (l.560–649) never produces a cone outside DEC-122's corrected category, so the correction loses nothing on the projective side.
labels.correction: DEC-127: MARKED in its corrected form (DEC-122's correction: the ℝ₊*-action on the cone is proper; DEC-124's objects: connected Hausdorff affine conical manifolds with a proper ℝ₊*-action against connected Hausdorff locally projective manifolds). The formalization of record is Benzecri.coneEquivalence : ConeCat (n+1) ≌ ProjCat n (Prop form Benzecri.baseFunctor_isEquivalence), functor V ↦ V/ℝ₊*, inverse Benzécri's F(B) = FJ(B)/ℛ, unit/counit the canonical unitIso/counitIso; the printed form, read over all Hausdorff connected cones, stays refuted for n ≥ 3 (Benzecri.not_essSurjAsPrinted_dim) as § 2 Prop. 2's finding carried over.

in_proof.sentence: « Nous allons définir F(B) comme un quotient de FJ(B), et FJ(B) s'identifiera avec J₁(F(B)) » (l.568); « on peut trouver une carte compatible et une seule d'un voisinage convenable de p qui soit composée d'un relèvement de ce voisinage sur un voisinage de (j, m) et de la projection … FJ(B) s'identifie donc avec l'espace des jets de cartes compatibles de F(B) » (l.598–604)
in_proof.ruling: DEC-127: to be formalized as its own bijection
in_proof.statement: FCone.fjJetHomeomorph n B : FJ n B ≃ₜ jets (GUR (n+1)) (RnO (n+1)) (FCone n B) — FJ(B) with the topology induced by J(B) × (ℝⁿ⁺¹ − {O}) is homeomorphic to J₁(F(B)) (the jets of F(B)'s affine conical structure, étalé topology), by (j, m) ↦ the jet at [(j, m)] of the compatible chart through (j, m) (fjJet; over a chart e of B with j = g∘jet_y e it is i(g)∘jet f_e, chart-independent by fjJet_eq). Compatibilities: source [(j, m)] (fjJet_fst), value m (value_fjJet), ℛ's g•(j, m) goes to i(g)∘· (fjJet_smul), and natural in B: under it φ' is composition with F(φ), fjJet(φ'(p)) ∘ F(φ) = fjJet(p) (jetCompEq_fjJet_pushFJ, « J₁(F(B₂))∘F(φ) ⊂ J₁(F(B₁)) », l.635). No Hausdorff, connectedness or countability hypothesis on B. A homeomorphism is the strongest form the sentences support (both sides carry their printed topologies).

in_proof.sentence: « on peut trouver un jet et un seul j₂ de J(B₂) tel que φ∘j₂ = j₁ » (l.639–640; [sic], read j₂∘φ = j₁, DEC-127)
in_proof.statement: existsUnique_pushJet hφ j₁ : ∃! j₂ : Jet B₂ (S n), j₂ ∈ J(B₂) ∧ JetCompEq φ j₂ j₁ (j₂ ∘ φ = j₁), the j₂ being pushJet hφ j₁; JetCompEq is independent of the representative of j₂ (JetCompEq.jet_comp); φ'(j₁, m) = (j₂, m) is pushFJ, and F(φ)[(j₁,m)] = [φ'(j₁,m)] (map_q, rfl).
